constraints: Every EN composite renders the exact complete original native name. JP consumes only original selected public semantic pieces.
English article THE/A/AN has no Japanese inflection; ARTICLE_YOUR alone retains explicit ownership. Full original argument union is retained.

User MGIVENNAME pieces require original creation provenance. Plain/called consumers accept an owned source descriptor only, preserving a future creator-certified literal proper name or translated proper/rank composite; missing provenance means whole English. Ghost/shopkeeper proper names remain source-contract literal cases. Descriptive species/adjectives need source-selected descriptors.
Shopkeeper normal recipe receives empty kind/invisible fields; titled recipe is selected only by the original extended-name branch.
Ghost original English possessive comes from the single original s_suffix result; JP ownership uses the original unsuffixed public proper name and adds no identity facts.
Current feminine/species labels are selected only by original returned pm_name pointer identity; ambiguity fails to whole English. No private gender metadata is exported.
Uppercase affects the already-completed native EN first byte once. JP grammar does not invent a capitalized variant.
Existing nethack.name.empty and invisible/saddled leaf IDs must remain paired in the installed catalog. Missing IDs, depth, limits or unknown producer yields whole original English.
No runtime rendered-English reverse mapping, rerun naming/RNG/state queries, private field getters or renderer state/RNG changes.
All source proposals require separate C compilation, semantic catalog verification and actual native/browser acceptance before runtime binding.
